positive.prompt: /melt-faces this repo and tell me if it's ready for the enterprise demo next week
Tear down our dashboard's UX and design like a top-tier product jury would, what's good and what's bad
Is this web app premium enough to sell to enterprise buyers? Give me an honest product critique

negative.prompt: Review this pull request diff before I merge it
Build a responsive settings page component with accessible form fields

evals.dialogue_justification: Grades the reach-honesty and candor rules, which govern what the reviewer says to the user when evidence is limited; the deliverable is the conversation, not file edits.
evals.prompt: /melt-faces https://example.com - this is our marketing site, we're pitching it to a Fortune 500 next week. Be honest.
evals.expected_output: A review explicitly limited to what a browser can see, with no source-code claims, n/a for dimensions that need the source, and an offer or question to get repo access
expectations: States up front that only the live site is reachable (no source), so findings cover visual, UX, content, accessibility, performance, and client-visible trust signals
Makes no claims about source code, tests, CI, or server-side behavior it could not observe
Scores dimensions that need source access as n/a (not visible) instead of guessing numbers
Asks the user, as a multiple-choice question with a recommended option, whether they can provide repo access or the buyer context
Uses direct, professional language without padding praise or hedging evidenced findings
